title_en: The Scientific Giant Who Changed the World
english_paragraphs: On 29 May 1919, as a total eclipse obscured the sun, two British expeditions photographed stars in its apparent vicinity. Arthur Eddington observed from Príncipe, an island off West Africa; Crommelin and Davidson from Sobral, in north-eastern Brazil. They were testing general relativity's bold prediction that the sun's gravity would deflect starlight.

On 6 November, at a joint meeting of the Royal Society and the Royal Astronomical Society, the findings were hailed as confirming it. The Times proclaimed a "Revolution in Science"; a New York Times headline read "Lights All Askew in the Heavens". Almost overnight, Einstein, eminent among physicists, became a global celebrity.

Stockholm proved harder to dazzle. The Nobel physics committee valued rigorous experimental confirmation, and committee member Allvar Gullstrand, a Nobel-winning eye specialist, deemed the empirical support for relativity insufficient. Since no nomination fulfilled Nobel's criteria, the 1921 prize was reserved for a year, as the statutes permit.

On 9 November 1922 the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences conferred it on Einstein, citing his services to theoretical physics, especially his discovery of the law of the photoelectric effect. That law, which governs how light ejects electrons from metal, helped underpin quantum theory. A letter the next day clarified that the prize took no account of relativity. Einstein, then aboard a steamer bound for Japan, would miss the December ceremony.

On 11 July 1923, in Gothenburg, Sweden, he delivered his Nobel lecture before a congress of Nordic scientists, devoting it to the fundamental ideas and problems of relativity. The theory the committee looked past reached a Nobel podium after all, carried there by the man the prize had honoured.
chinese_paragraphs: 1919年5月29日，日全食遮住太阳时，两支英国考察队拍摄了天空中看似靠近太阳的恒星。阿瑟·爱丁顿在西非外海的普林西比岛观测，克罗姆林和戴维森则在巴西东北部的索布拉尔观测。他们要检验广义相对论的一个大胆预言：太阳的引力会让星光发生偏折。
同年11月6日，在英国皇家学会和皇家天文学会的联席会议上，这些观测结果被盛赞为证实了该预言。《泰晤士报》宣告“科学革命”；《纽约时报》则以“天上的光全歪了”为标题。几乎一夜之间，原本已在物理学界享有盛名的爱因斯坦，变成了全球名人。
斯德哥尔摩的诺奖评审却没那么容易被打动。诺贝尔物理学委员会重视严格的实验证实，而委员阿尔瓦·古尔斯特兰德——一位获得过诺奖的眼科专家——认为相对论的实证支持不足。由于没有一项提名符合诺贝尔规定的标准，1921年的物理学奖按照章程保留一年。
1922年11月9日，瑞典皇家科学院把这个奖授予爱因斯坦，表彰他对理论物理学的贡献，尤其是发现光电效应定律。这一定律揭示光如何使金属释放电子，并帮助奠定了量子理论的基础。授奖决定次日的一封信明确说明，奖项并未考虑相对论。爱因斯坦当时乘轮船前往日本，因此未能参加12月的颁奖典礼。
1923年7月11日，爱因斯坦在瑞典哥德堡的北欧科学家大会上发表诺贝尔演讲，专讲相对论的基本思想与问题。那个被委员会绕开的理论，终究登上了诺贝尔讲台；把它带上去的，正是获得这个奖的人。

Warm ivory paper dominates; subdued eucalyptus and sage greens structure the composition; restrained buttery lemon-yellow and dusty terracotta accents. Calm, comfortable, refined, credible drawing and natural anatomy. An airy coherent composition with one clear story focal point and at most two supporting details, generous breathing room at all edges and softly feathered painted edges into ivory. Human figures treated with dignity; no grotesque caricature, no sensational violence or visible injuries. For disasters, emphasize the setting, evidence or human response without graphic suffering. Absolutely no typography, captions, letters, numbers, logos, watermarks, diagram labels, fake writing or invented charts anywhere. Do not render invisible forces as literal magic. Avoid corporate vector icons, slick 3D rendering and childish cartoon style. High-quality, print-ready visual storytelling, matching a warm ivory-and-sage adult watercolor booklet.

ARTICLE-SPECIFIC SCENE:
A refined scientific still life showing the photoelectric effect, the specific discovery named in Einstein's Nobel citation, rather than a generic portrait or the bending of starlight. On a quiet early-20th-century laboratory bench stands a credible brass-and-clear-glass photoelectric cell: inside its evacuated glass chamber, ordinary light from a shaded period laboratory lamp falls on a dull metal plate facing a collecting electrode. A few simple wires lead to an understated closed measuring box, its face turned away so there are no scales, letters or invented readings. The clear focal point is the illuminated metal surface within the glass cell; show only real lamp illumination, NO visible electrons, flying glowing particles, magic rays or scientific arrows. No scientist is present, so the picture does not falsely depict Einstein personally performing an experiment. One plain folded sheet seen from its blank reverse is the only secondary object, subtly evoking an award notice without showing a medal, logo or writing. Warm ivory background, sage-grey glass shadows and restrained lemon lamplight, sophisticated editorial watercolor.
